name: Catch a conversion error
intro: An exception is a problem raised while code runs. int("hello") raises ValueError. try/except lets you handle that specific problem with a useful message instead of stopping the program.
prompt: Use try to convert invalid whole-number text with int and print the number. Add except ValueError with a helpful printed message.
why: You used catch a conversion error in working Python.

name: Keep going after recovery
intro: A handled exception does not have to end the program. After try/except finishes, Python continues at the next statement outside it, whether try succeeded or the error was handled.
prompt: Catch ValueError from int on invalid text, print a recovery message, then print a different message outside try/except.
why: You used keep going after recovery in working Python.

name: Only on success: else
intro: try/except can also have else. Its block runs only when the try block finishes without an exception. Use it for work that needs a successfully converted value.
prompt: Convert valid whole-number text inside try. Handle ValueError with a message, and print the converted number plus 1 inside else.
why: You used only on success: else in working Python.

name: Cleanup with finally
intro: finally is a block for work that must run when Python leaves try, whether it succeeded or raised an exception. It is often used for cleanup. Here a printed message makes the timing visible.
prompt: Use try with an invalid int conversion, except ValueError with a printed recovery, and finally with a printed cleanup message.
hint:
try:
    number = int("bad")
    print(number)
except ValueError:
    print("Invalid number")
finally:
    print("Check ended")
why: You used cleanup with finally in working Python.

name: Handle a missing file
intro: Reading a nonexistent file raises FileNotFoundError. You can catch that exact error and explain what happened. In this app the practice workspace resets every Run, so this example starts with no saved.txt.
prompt: Try reading a missing practice filename in "r" mode and printing its content. Catch FileNotFoundError and print a helpful message. Do not create that file first.
why: You used handle a missing file in working Python.

name: Handle different problems
intro: One try can have several except blocks. Python selects the first matching handler. Invalid numeric text and division by zero are different problems, so give each a clear message.
prompt: Inside try, read int(input()) and print 12 divided by that number. Add separate except ValueError and except ZeroDivisionError blocks with helpful messages.
why: You used handle different problems in working Python.

name: A safer number reader
intro: Combine input, conversion and success-only work. A good response depends on what happened: explain invalid text, or use the valid number. End with a message in either case.
prompt: Read int(input()) inside try. Catch ValueError with a message. In else print the converted number plus 1. Add finally with a completion message.
why: You used a safer number reader in working Python.
